summary: A Rowan County, Kentucky tower dated to 1934 (builder disputed), abandoned, damaged by arson in 2008, restored, and now rented for overnight stays by the Route 377 fire department.

facts.design: 80-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7x7 cab (register says metal cab; county says wooden)

access.note: Hike in on foot past a vehicle gate; overnight stays are booked online through Morehead-Rowan County Tourism

visit.trail_note: About 1.2 miles on foot past a vehicle gate, per The Outbound

events.note: Wooden tower; county credits the CCC, while the register credits the U.S. Forest Service
Replaced with steel, per the county tower page
Mid-1970s per the county news post (approximate year); the county tower page says the Forest Service stopped using it in the 1960s
Visit report of October 18, 2022 says the tower is now available for rental

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The county credits the Civilian Conservation Corps (1934 wooden tower, steel in 1935). The register and The Outbound credit the U.S. Forest Service. The sources do not reconcile the builder.
The register and the county tower page give 80 feet. The county news post says 35 feet, which appears to be an error because two sources give 80 feet. The story uses 80 feet.

The county tower page says the Forest Service stopped using the tower in the 1960s; the county news post says aircraft replaced lookouts by the mid-1970s. The event year 1975 is an approximation of the news post's date.

notes_for_editor: Builder, cab material and abandonment date are disputed; the 35-foot figure looks like an error. Access 'public' rests on The Outbound's hike notes (undated) and the county's rental post; confirm with Route 377 before any visit advice goes out. Staffing comes from NHLR visit reports dated 2008, 2016 and 2022. No photos recorded. The county's 'replace with steel' wording is quoted as printed.
